population.span: involving patients with both severe CAP and a high inflammatory response, defined by a level of C-reactive protein (CRP) >15 mg/dL on admission

endpoint.span: In-hospital mortality was a secondary outcome and adverse events were assessed.

estimate.span: In-hospital mortality did not differ between the 2 groups (6 patients [10%] in the methylprednisolone group vs 9 patients [15%] in the placebo group; P = .37); the difference between groups was 5% (95% CI, -6% to 17%).

ci.span: In-hospital mortality did not differ between the 2 groups (6 patients [10%] in the methylprednisolone group vs 9 patients [15%] in the placebo group; P = .37); the difference between groups was 5% (95% CI, -6% to 17%).

treatment_strategy.span: Patients were randomized to receive either an intravenous bolus of 0.5 mg/kg per 12 hours of methylprednisolone (n = 61) or placebo (n = 59) for 5 days started within 36 hours of hospital admission.

follow_up.span: Adverse events and mortality were recorded during the hospital stay.

absent_reason: analysis_set: No held source explicitly identifies the analysis set for the original abstract's mortality difference and confidence interval. The full texts describe post hoc populations; their ITT or per-protocol labels cannot establish the analysis set of this estimate.
served_mismatch: The served mortality event counts agree with the original abstract. However, its reported effect and CI are a difference of 5% (95% CI, -6% to 17%), not an RR. The served ITT label is not explicitly established for this estimate. Randomized arm sizes are stated, but are not explicitly identified as mortality-analysis denominators.

candidate_rejections.why: Adjusted effects from an antibiotic-defined post hoc subset, not the original whole-trial mortality comparison or an RR.

candidate_rejections.span: Corticosteroid treatment reduced the risk of treatment failure (odds ratio, 0.34 [95% CI, 0.14 to 0.87]; P = .02).
candidate_rejections.why: This estimate concerns the treatment-failure composite, not in-hospital mortality.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Hospitalized patients with severe CAP and high inflammation fall within the question's CAP population; registry eligibility establishes adulthood. ITT applicability is separately unverified.
entry_population_matches_question.span: ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 18 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL

notes: Registry evidence was used for adult eligibility. The original abstract supplies the whole-trial mortality estimate and CI; held full texts are post hoc reports. The printed positive difference is preserved without reversing its sign or converting it to RR. Randomized sizes of 61 and 59 were not inferred to be analysis denominators.
